LESSON: READING 10.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.2: Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why should we read at the right speed? 2. What should we do to remember what we read?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read factual texts of about 320 words related to the theme for comprehension,
2. apply appropriate reading habits in reading factual texts of about 320 words for information,
3. realise the importance of reading for comprehension and information. The learner is guided to: text, questions from a variety of texts, story with peers, and pick out specific information, information related to the theme. we read at the right speed? we do to remember what we read?

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading.
2. Explain Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Try this activity: read factual texts in print and non- print formats,
4. Show that you can: read factual texts of about 320 words related to the theme for comprehension,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why should we read at the right speed? 2. What should we do to remember what we read?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read factual texts in print and non- print formats,
2. Discuss and role play events in a story with peers,

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. read factual texts of about 320 words related to the theme for comprehension,
2. apply appropriate reading habits in reading factual texts of about 320 words for information,
3. realise the importance of reading for comprehension and information. The learner is guided to: text, questions from a variety of texts, story with peers, and pick out specific information, information related to the theme. we read at the right speed? we do to remember what we read?
